3.2.value: Current cycle (N-23C3A filed 2026-05-08): offer period 5/8/2026-5/29/2026; Repurchase Request Deadline 4:00 p.m. ET on 5/29/2026; Repurchase Pricing Date the SAME day, 5/29/2026 (NAV as of NYSE close); payment within seven (7) calendar days of the Pricing Date; reference NAV on 5/5/2026 was $10.39/share; offer size up to 5% of outstanding shares; no repurchase fee (cell 2.7). WITHDRAWAL RIGHTS: requests may be withdrawn or modified any time before the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline. PRORATION: if more than 5% is tendered, 'the Fund may, but is not required to, repurchase up to an additional two percent (2%)'; if it does not, or if more than 7% is tendered, repurchase is pro rata; de minimis exception - accounts under $2,500 tendering all shares may be accepted before proration; unfilled requests roll to the next quarterly offer with no priority. SUSPENSION/POSTPONEMENT: only by vote of a majority of the Board including a majority of independent Trustees, in four enumerated circumstances (RIC-status loss, NYSE/principal-market closure or restricted trading, emergency making disposal or valuation impracticable, or SEC order). PROSPECTUS FRAMEWORK (486BPOS): quarterly offers of 5%-25% set by Board (fundamental policy); request deadline must fall 'no less than 21 and no more than 42 days after the Fund sends a notification' of the offer; pricing date no later than the 14th day after the deadline (next business day if not a business day) - so a shareholder may irrevocably tender before knowing the price when pricing follows the deadline; partial tenders must keep a $2,500 minimum balance or the Fund may repurchase the whole account; sub-100-share accounts tendering all shares may be accepted before proration; oversubscribed offers may add an 'Estate Offer' tranche for estates.

6.2.value: Objectives: primary — consistent current income; secondary — capital preservation. 80% policy: under normal market conditions at least 80% of assets (net assets plus borrowings for investment purposes) in loans to companies ('corporate loans'), accessed through seven printed routes: (i) direct loans originated by non-bank lenders; (ii) notes/pass-through obligations on direct loans; (iii) asset-backed securities on pools of direct loans; (iv) companies and/or private investment funds (3(c)(1)/3(c)(7)) primarily holding direct loans; (v) high yield securities; (vi) bank loans; (vii) SPVs and/or joint ventures holding loans or credit-like securities. Printed limit: investments in 3(c)(1)/3(c)(7) hedge funds and private equity funds limited to no more than 15% of assets. Non-U.S. investments permitted; currency fluctuations 'intended to be hedged through the use of currency derivatives or other instruments.' Other instruments: preferred securities, convertible securities, derivatives (options, swaps, futures contracts, forward agreements, reverse repurchase agreements and other similar transactions) for hedging and investment purposes, ETFs and other investment companies, warrants/equity of borrowers, Warehouses (pre-CLO/CDO financing structures); use subject to Rule 18f-4 (VaR leverage limit / derivatives risk management program unless limited derivatives user). Actually held per N-CSR at 3/31/2026: forward foreign currency exchange contracts and interest rate swap contracts (hedging fixed-rate debt).

6.3.value: Conflicts: dedicated 'CONFLICTS OF INTEREST' section — Investment Manager and affiliates advise other vehicles with similar strategies that may compete for opportunities and may co-invest; shareholders deemed to acknowledge/waive certain conflict claims; valuation conflict disclosed ('participation of the investment professionals of the Investment Manager in the Fund's valuation process could result in a conflict of interest as the Investment Management Fee is based on the value of the Fund's assets'). Co-investment order: NOT held as of this prospectus — risk factor 'FAILURE TO OBTAIN CO-INVESTMENT EXEMPTIVE RELIEF' states the Fund and Investment Manager 'may seek' Section 17(d) exemptive relief and 'There is no assurance that the Fund or the Investment Manager will receive such exemptive relief.' Affiliated/related-party amounts (N-CSR FY2026, filed 2026-06-08): Investment Management fees $309,391,914 (1.00% annualized of daily net assets; payable $6,861,054 at 3/31/2026); Note 12 affiliated investments — FBLC Senior Loan Fund LLC (value $53,105,189 at 3/31/2026; return of capital $(20,022,363); dividend income $6,690,429) and Capstone Lending LLC (purchases $23,632,903; value $23,908,620), both 50/50 unconsolidated JVs (with Franklin BSP Lending Corporation and Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund respectively).
